people.name: Hugh Trenchard, 1st Viscount Trenchard
people.nameZh: 第一代特倫查德子爵休·特倫查德

heading.en: An infantryman who paid to learn to fly

body.zh-Hant: 特倫查德原本是步兵出身，1912年學飛時只是個前途看來不太光明的少校。他曾兩度沒通過陸軍入學考試，約二十歲時才勉強過關，成為少尉並派往印度。皇家飛行團1912年成立時不收四十歲以上的人，上司說他又高又老，他卻請了兩週假、自費受訓。大戰爆發前的兩年，他開的課程培養出皇家飛行團陸上部門的大部分軍官。
body.en: Trenchard began his service career as an infantryman and was a major by 1912, when he learned to fly. He twice failed the army entrance exams and passed at about twenty, becoming a lieutenant posted to India. The Royal Flying Corps of 1912 took no one over 40, and his commanding officer told him he was too tall and too old, but he took two weeks of leave and paid for his own instruction. In the two years before the war his courses turned out most of the officers for the corps’ land-based branch.

heading.en: France and the Battle of Loos

body.zh-Hant: 1914年11月，特倫查德帶著皇家飛行團三個作戰聯隊之一前往法國。1915年1月初黑格召見他，說明3月進攻訥沙佩勒的祕密計畫，這場進攻並不成功。1915年8月，他成為全體駐法英國空軍的指揮官。9月25日起的盧斯戰役中，他的機群先以三天轟炸鐵路樞紐，並首次保留部分中隊作預備隊；戰後他晉升，英國遠征軍總司令弗倫奇在戰報中特別表揚鐵路轟炸。1915年底損失劇增後，他規定偵察機須有至少三架護航。
body.en: Trenchard went to France in November 1914 commanding one of the Royal Flying Corps’ three operational wings. In early January 1915 Haig summoned him and revealed secret plans for a March offensive at Neuve Chapelle, which was not a success. In August 1915 he became commander of all British air forces in France. At Loos, where the ground attack began on 25 September 1915, his squadrons bombed rail junctions for three days and, for the first time, he held some squadrons in reserve. The battle brought him a promotion and a citation from the BEF commander-in-chief praising the railway bombing. After heavy losses in late 1915 he required reconnaissance aircraft to be escorted by at least three others.

heading.zh-Hant: 空軍參謀長與轟炸理論
heading.en: Chief of the Air Staff and the bombing doctrine

body.zh-Hant: 1918年4月，皇家空軍成立才兩週，特倫查德在首任空軍參謀長任上僅四個月便憤而辭職，他歸咎於總部政治。1918年夏天，他的轟炸部隊成為焦點，策略是把攻擊分散到德國各處，偏好的目標是鐵路與高爐。1919年，邱吉爾召他回任空軍參謀長，直到1929年退休。戰後他力保皇家空軍作為獨立軍種的存續，主張下一場大戰單靠轟炸即可取勝；牛津辭典指出，這個主張在二戰中證明大錯。
body.en: In April 1918, two weeks after the RAF was formed, Trenchard abruptly quit as the first chief of the Air Staff after only four months, blaming headquarters politics. In the summer of 1918 his bomber force was the focus of attention; his strategy was to spread attacks across Germany, favouring railways and blast furnaces. In 1919 Churchill recalled him as chief of the Air Staff, a post he kept until retiring in 1929. After 1918 he fought to preserve the RAF’s independence, claiming the next major war could be won by bombing alone, a claim the Oxford entry says proved hopelessly wrong in the Second World War.

heading.en: Commissioner of Police of the Metropolis

body.zh-Hant: 上議院1956年的悼詞提到，特倫查德後來出任首都警察總監，在蘇格蘭場引進新人與新方法；悼詞列出他任內推動亨頓警察學院、短期服役招募制度，以及警隊的科學化。發言的議員說他為這個職位付出了四年，離任時留下一支滿意且高效的警隊。悼詞另稱克蘭威爾與霍爾頓兩處空軍設施都是他的創建。
body.en: The House of Lords tribute of 1956 recalls that he later served as Commissioner of Police for the Metropolis, bringing fresh men and fresh methods to Scotland Yard. It credits him with the Hendon Police College, the short-service recruiting scheme and scientific methods in the force, and says he gave four years to that office, leaving a contented and efficient force. The tribute also calls Cranwell and Halton his creations.

heading.zh-Hant: 出身、早年軍旅到埃及駐軍
heading.en: Birth, early service and the Egypt command

body.zh-Hant: 拜恩1862年9月11日生於巴尼特的羅斯罕公園，是第二代斯特拉福伯爵之子。1879年12月12日他在第二密德薩斯民兵團任少尉，後來轉入第十驃騎兵團；1884年在蘇丹塔邁一役中被通報嘉獎。1899年南非戰爭爆發後，他抵達南非並指揮新編的南非輕騎兵團。1909年4月1日晉升少將，1910年10月9日出任東盎格利亞師長，1912年10月30日到開羅接掌英軍埃及駐軍。
body.en: Byng was born on 11 September 1862 at Wrotham Park, Barnet, son of the 2nd Earl of Strafford. He became a second lieutenant in the 2nd Middlesex Militia on 12 December 1879, later joined the 10th Hussars, and was mentioned in despatches at the battle of Tamai in 1884. In the South African war he arrived on 9 November and commanded the newly raised South African Light Horse. Promoted major-general on 1 April 1909, he took the East Anglian Division on 9 October 1910 and assumed command of British forces in Egypt on 30 October 1912.

heading.en: World War I: Cavalry Corps and Gallipoli

body.zh-Hant: 1914年8月大戰爆發，拜恩所部被編入第一軍，十至十一月在比利時打了第一次伊珀爾戰役。1915年4月他暫代騎兵軍軍長，次月在第二次伊珀爾戰役期間成為正式軍長並暫升中將。同年8月他受命統率第九軍，24日抵達蘇弗拉灣；他很快認定英軍處境無望，12月初撤退命令下達後，行動完成時沒有損失人員、牲畜或裝備。他因加里波利之役獲KCB，之後短暫指揮第十七軍。
body.en: After war broke out in August 1914 Byng’s division was assigned to I Corps and fought at the first battle of Ypres in October–November 1914. In April 1915 he took temporary command of the Cavalry Corps and a month later, during the second battle of Ypres, became its regular commander and a temporary lieutenant-general. In August 1915 he was sent to command IX Corps, arriving at Suvla Bay on 24 August; when the order to withdraw came in early December the evacuation was completed without loss of men, animals or equipment. He received a KCB for Gallipoli and then briefly commanded XVII Corps.

heading.en: The Canadian Corps and Vimy Ridge

body.zh-Hant: 1916年5月下旬，拜恩奉命接替奧爾德森指揮加拿大軍，並升為中將。山姆·休斯要他任命自己的兒子接掌第三師，他拒絕，改任命利普西特。同年9月加拿大軍在庫塞萊特戰役傷亡逾七千人。1917年1月他受命奪取維米嶺全部山脊，砲擊從3月20日起，攻擊於4月9日清晨5時30分展開，至4月14日北端高地被占；攻方傷亡10,602人，其中3,598人陣亡。同年6月，黑格命他轉任第三軍團，加拿大軍由柯里接任。
body.en: In late May 1916 Byng was ordered to replace Alderson as commander of the Canadian Corps, with promotion to lieutenant-general. When Sam Hughes ordered him to give the 3rd Division to Hughes’s son, he refused and appointed Lipsett. In September the Canadians took more than 7,000 casualties at Courcelette. In January 1917 he was ordered to capture the whole crest of Vimy Ridge; the bombardment began on 20 March, the attack on 9 April at 5:30 a.m., and the northern tip fell on 14 April, at a cost of 10,602 casualties including 3,598 killed. In June 1917 Haig ordered him to take over the Third Army and Currie succeeded him.

heading.en: Third Army and Cambrai

body.zh-Hant: 1917年10月中旬，拜恩的第三軍團受命領頭進攻康布雷。他把維米的預演手法用到這裡，加入空中掩護與大量坦克，並刻意不先行砲擊以保突然性。11月20日黎明攻擊展開，初期在六英里正面推進三到四英里，但德軍增援後奪回大部分地面。11月23日他升為上將。1918年春季德軍攻勢中，第三軍團負責防守北法二十八英里戰線；到1918年11月11日停戰，第三軍團死傷失蹤逾十一萬五千人。
body.en: In mid-October 1917 Byng’s Third Army was given the lead in the attack at Cambrai. Drawing on Vimy, he rehearsed his troops, used aircraft cover and heavy tank support, and planned no preliminary bombardment to keep surprise. The assault began at dawn on 20 November and at first advanced three to four miles on a six-mile front, but German reserves recovered much of the ground. He was raised to full general on 23 November. In 1918 the Third Army defended 28 miles of line in northern France during the German spring offensive, and by the armistice on 11 November 1918 it had lost more than 115,000 men killed, wounded or missing.

heading.en: Postwar service and Governor General of Canada

body.zh-Hant: 戰後拜恩於1919年7月接任聯合軍人基金主席，為此辭去軍職；同年8月受封貴族。1921年6月3日宣布出任加拿大總督，8月2日領到總督與三軍總司令的任命狀，8月10日抵魁北克。任內他在1926年的金—拜恩事件中拒絕了首相金要求解散國會的請求，金隨即辭職。他在1926年10月被封為子爵。
body.en: After the war Byng accepted the chairmanship of the United Services Fund in July 1919, resigning from the army to do so, and was raised to the peerage in August. His appointment as governor general of Canada was announced on 3 June 1921; he received his commission on 2 August and arrived at Quebec on 10 August. In 1926, in the King–Byng affair, he refused Prime Minister King’s request and King immediately resigned. He was made a viscount in October 1926.

body.zh-Hant: 1928年6月，內政大臣先向拜恩徵詢大都會警察總監人選，隨後認定他本人最合適，任命於7月2日公布。1930年7月26日他心臟病發，次年10月辭去警察總監職務。1932年10月，他晉升陸軍元帥。1935年6月6日清晨，拜恩在索普廳去世。
body.en: In June 1928 the home secretary asked Byng for advice on the Metropolitan Police chief commissioner and then decided he was himself the best candidate; his appointment was announced on 2 July. He had a heart attack on 26 July 1930 and resigned the commissionership in October 1931. He was promoted field marshal in October 1932 and died early on 6 June 1935.

heading.en: Origins and staff service in the First World War

body.zh-Hant: 迪爾1881年12月25日生於愛爾蘭阿馬郡盧爾甘，1900年8月進桑赫斯特皇家軍事學院，1901年5月7日獲任萊因斯特團軍官，同年9月10日起參加波耳戰爭。第一次大戰中，他1914年11月5日任法國戰場第二十五步兵旅的旅參謀長，1917年12月16日起任法國總司令部作戰處一級參謀，1918年3月27日升作戰處總參謀准將；美軍官方戰史稱他在大戰末期是黑格元帥的作戰參謀長。
body.en: Dill was born on 25 December 1881 at Lurgan, County Armagh, entered Sandhurst in August 1900, was commissioned into the Leinster Regiment on 7 May 1901 and served in the Boer War from 10 September 1901. In the First World War he became Brigade Major of the 25th Infantry Brigade in France on 5 November 1914, a GSO1 (Operations) at GHQ France from 16 December 1917, and Brigadier-General, General Staff (Operations) on 27 March 1918; the US official history calls him Haig’s Brigadier General Staff Operations near the end of the war.

On 8 September 1936 he became General Officer Commanding Palestine and Trans-Jordan as a lieutenant-general, and on 12 October 1937 GOC-in-C Home Command at Aldershot.

Danchev notes he was made CIGS in the May 1940 crisis as the Dunkirk evacuations were about to begin. The US official history says he served as CIGS to the end of 1941; on 19 November 1941 his retirement as CIGS and his designation as Governor of Bombay were announced.

heading.en: Washington and death

body.zh-Hant: 1942年1月，迪爾出任英國駐華盛頓聯合參謀代表團團長，並任聯合參謀長委員會的英方資深成員；公開的祕密是他代表身兼國防大臣的邱吉爾。他與馬歇爾1941年8月在大西洋會議初識，其後結為摯友。1944年11月4日他在華盛頓去世；11月8日華盛頓特區降半旗，華盛頓大教堂舉行追思，隨後安葬阿靈頓國家公墓，1950年11月1日當地為他豎立紀念像。
body.en: In January 1942 Dill became head of the British Joint Staff Mission in Washington and senior British member of the Combined Chiefs of Staff; it was an open secret that he represented Churchill as Minister of Defence. He and Marshall first met at the Atlantic Conference in August 1941 and became close friends. Dill died in Washington on 4 November 1944; on 8 November flags in the District of Columbia flew at half-mast and a memorial service was held at Washington Cathedral before burial at Arlington, where a statue was unveiled on 1 November 1950.

body.zh-Hant: 丹切夫（Danchev）寫道，1940年5月敦克爾克撤退即將展開之際，迪爾出任帝國總參謀長；他曾花三個月在地中海一帶旅行，爭取希臘與土耳其支持對抗軸心國。1941年12月珍珠港事件後，他被調往美國，出任英國駐華盛頓聯合參謀代表團團長。馬歇爾基金會的文章則記載，迪爾曾向倫敦示警：若否決「大錘」（SLEDGEHAMMER，1942年在西北歐登陸）而改採「GYMNAST」（北非登陸，來源拼作 GYNMAST），後果為何；1943年11至12月開羅／德黑蘭會議期間，馬歇爾曾提議由迪爾出任「霸王」（OVERLORD，西北歐登陸）最高統帥，邱吉爾對此不滿。
body.en: Alex Danchev writes that Dill was made Chief of the Imperial General Staff in May 1940, as the evacuations from Dunkirk were about to get under way, and that he spent three months travelling in the Mediterranean canvassing Greek and Turkish support against the Axis. After Pearl Harbor in December 1941 he was sent to the United States as head of the British Joint Staff Mission in Washington. The Marshall Foundation article records that Dill alerted London to the consequences of rejecting SLEDGEHAMMER (a 1942 landing in northwest Europe) in favour of GYMNAST (a North African landing, spelled GYNMAST in the source), and that during the Cairo/Teheran Conferences of November-December 1943 Marshall suggested Dill as Supreme Commander for OVERLORD, which Churchill resented.

body.en: Pound was born on 29 August 1877 and began his naval career at thirteen. In the first month of the Great War he stressed that aircraft must work with the navy against submarines; as a captain he became naval assistant to First Sea Lord Fisher. By 1916 he commanded the battleship HMS Colossus in the Grand Fleet, which at Jutland sank the German cruiser Wiesbaden and the destroyer V48, and he brought the damaged ship back to Scapa Flow. The official history adds that as a captain he was Director of the Plans Division of the Naval Staff.

In August 1932 he returned to the Admiralty as Second Sea Lord for three years, and in September 1935 went back to the Mediterranean Fleet as Commander-in-Chief, a post he had held for three and a half years when recalled in June 1939.

He was to carry a very heavy burden through four years of war. The reviewer calls his great accomplishment his near single-minded concentration on the Battle of the Atlantic, and says he persuaded Admiral King to assign an escort carrier to Atlantic convoys, closing the air gap.

body.zh-Hant: 1941年12月，他同意派不幸的Z部隊前往遠東，結果威爾斯親王號與反擊號被擊沉。1942年夏天，PQ 17船團繞行斯堪地那維亞前往阿爾漢格爾，他親自負責下令船團疏散，之後船團損失二十三艘船，護航艦艇則毫髮無傷。他在魁北克會議期間中風，宣布自己不適任並向邱吉爾請辭；1943年10月21日特拉法加日，他在倫敦的醫院逝世，繼任者是A.B.坎寧安。
body.en: In December 1941 he went along with the dispatch of the ill-fated Force Z to the Far East, which cost Prince of Wales and Repulse. In summer 1942 convoy PQ 17 went round Scandinavia to Archangel; he took personal responsibility for ordering its dispersal, and the convoy lost twenty-three ships while the naval escorts escaped unscathed. A paralytic stroke during the Quebec Conference led him to declare himself unfit for duty and resign to Churchill; he died in a London hospital on Trafalgar Day, 21 October 1943, leaving A. B. Cunningham as his successor.

body.zh-Hant: 1914年他任第2阿爾及利亞步兵團營長，在阿拉斯受傷：官方人物檔記載，他的營獨自擋住敵軍一個師近二十小時，1915年10月5日腿部負傷，後被俘並在英戈爾施塔特結識戴高樂上尉。1919至1920年他加入法國駐阿拉伯軍事使團，聖雷莫會議（1920年4月）後出任大馬士革邦總督。1923至1925年任駐君士坦丁堡武官；1925年6至10月參與里夫戰爭，次年到黎凡特主張敘利亞、黎巴嫩獨立；1927年他轉任第6阿爾及利亞步兵團團長。
body.en: In 1914 Catroux was a battalion commander in the 2nd Algerian Tirailleurs and was wounded in the leg at Arras on 5 October 1915 after holding a division at bay for nearly 20 hours with his battalion alone. Captured, he met Captain de Gaulle at Ingolstadt. In 1919–1920 he was in the French military mission to Arabia and, after the San Remo conference of April 1920, was named governor of the State of Damascus. He was military attaché in Constantinople in 1923–1925, took part in the Rif war from June to October, in 1926 advocated Syrian and Lebanese independence under High Commissioner de Jouvenel, and in 1927 took command of the 6th Algerian Tirailleurs at Tlemcen.

heading.en: Joining Free France and the Levant

body.zh-Hant: 1940年8月，卡特魯響應六一八號召，投向戴高樂；9月17日抵倫敦，邱吉爾提議由他領導自由法國，他謝絕。1941年6月，他以戴高樂之名宣布敘利亞與黎巴嫩獨立；敘利亞戰役後，1941年7月19日他受命為自由法國駐黎凡特高級專員。1942年11月25日他被任命為法軍指揮官，1943年3至6月兼任阿爾及利亞總督，並在1943年6月3日成立的法蘭西民族解放委員會中擔任委員。
body.en: In August 1940 Catroux, who had heard the appeal of 18 June, rallied to de Gaulle; on 17 September he reached London, where Churchill proposed that he lead Free France and he declined. In June 1941 he proclaimed the independence of Syria and Lebanon in de Gaulle’s name; after the Syrian campaign he was named High Commissioner of Free France in the Levant on 19 July. He was named commander of the French forces on 25 November 1942, served as governor general of Algeria from March to June 1943, and was named a member of the French Committee of National Liberation on its creation on 3 June 1943.

body.en: In November 1943 he became Commissioner of State for Muslim Affairs, and in September 1944 de Gaulle named him Minister of State for North Africa. He died on 21 December 1969 at the Val-de-Grâce hospital.
